Criteria.TestCondition: The user can pause, stop, hide, or control the frequency of automatically updating content.
DisabilityImpact: With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities
Criteria.TesterComment: This test could not be performed: We watched this page for 6.5 seconds without touching it, looking for content that is still changing by itself after 5 seconds, like a carousel, ticker or counter. Nothing was, but we saw signs that the page may update by itself: it sets a timer of 86400 s, longer than we watched (when we ran the page's clock past it, the page asked its server for something, and our copy of the page cannot show what the server would send). A person should watch the page for a minute to see whether anything keeps changing.

Criteria.TestCondition: All functionality can be accessed and executed using only the keyboard.
Criteria.TesterComment: We could not finish this test, so a person needs to check it. The page has an embedded frame we could not read that we cannot check automatically; please check it works with the keyboard. The page has something that reacts to mouse movement, touch or the scroll wheel that we cannot check automatically; please check it works with the keyboard. Only the first 40 elements were checked for menus that open when the mouse rests on them. We looked for: things a mouse can click that the keyboard never reaches, including inside frames; menus that open when the mouse rests on them; custom controls that ignore Enter and Space; and tooltips with information found nowhere else. Results are for the browser used (version 153.0.8010.12).

Criteria.TestCondition: There is no keyboard trap.
Criteria.TesterComment: We moved through the whole page with Tab and with Shift+Tab, and keyboard focus never got trapped. The page seems to load more content as you scroll, and the recording could not show all of it; content after the feed was reached only by Shift+Tab from the end.

Criteria.TestCondition: The focus order preserves the meaning and operability of the web page.
DisabilityImpact: With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities
Criteria.TesterComment: Keyboard focus moves through the page in an order that follows how it reads, forward and backward. The focus order departs from the reading order (focus jumps back up the page from "Science" (link) to "NASA's Athena supercomputer." (link); focus jumps back up the page from "Science" (link) to "Image of Mercury taken by NASA's MESSENGER miss..." (link); focus jumps back up the page from "Earth Science" (link) to "opacities" (link); focus jumps back up the page from "Heliophysics" (link) to "Artist's impression of a supermassive black hole." (link); focus jumps back up the page from "Earth Science" (link) to "James Webb Space Telescope image of a sliver of..." (link); focus jumps back up the page from "Contact" (link) to "DATA SEARCH" (link); focus jumps back up the page from "Science Explorer Digital Library" (link) to "DATA SITES" (link); focus jumps back up the page from "Planetary Science" (link) to "ACROSS" (link)), but it still makes sense: cards grid, parts together. If you disagree, tell your assistant.
